lines.text: A plugin bundles skills, commands, hooks, subagents and MCP servers into one install.
lines.say: A plugin bundles skills, commands, hooks, subagents and M C P servers into one install.

lines.text: You get them from marketplaces, which are catalogs of plugins.
Install one with /plugin install, its name, an @, and the marketplace.
lines.say: Install one with slash plugin install, its name, an at sign, and the marketplace.

lines.text: Its skills arrive with the plugin's name in front, like /superpowers:brainstorming.
lines.say: Its skills arrive with the plugin's name in front, like slash superpowers colon brainstorming.

lines.text: A plugin can be on for you alone,|or for everyone in the repository, through its committed settings.
Four worth installing, each a different layer.
Superpowers is skills: brainstorm, plan, test first, debug, verify.|This article was planned with its brainstorming skill.
Playwright is MCP: a real browser the agent drives,|like opening your dev server at phone width and taking a screenshot.
lines.say: Playwright is M C P: a real browser the agent drives, like opening your dev server at phone width and taking a screenshot.

lines.text: Security guidance is hooks: it warns about risky patterns as files change,|and reviews the diff when the agent stops.
Claude Code setup is a skill that reads your repository|and recommends automations for each layer, without changing a thing.
Run on this portfolio, it suggested a hook that enforces its Docker-only rule,|and a /verify skill that runs all five checks.
lines.say: Run on this portfolio, it suggested a hook that enforces its Docker-only rule, and a slash verify skill that runs all five checks.

lines.text: A plugin loads into every session and can run code on your machine,|so read its hooks before you install it.
Install only what you use: every skill description costs context.
The signal to build your own: a second repository needs the same setup.
Codex has plugins too, shared with ChatGPT.
